newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end higher on buying of leaders.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end higher on buying of leaders.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange ended higher Thursday on local buying of leaders which had suffered corrections in previous sessions, brokers said.
They predicted a stable session Friday given the lack of economic news moving the market.
"Today the bolsa was marked by aggressive buys of leaders which suffered a strong fall in recent days," said Hugo Elcorobarrutia, of MGS brokerage.
The General Index edged up 0.94 percent to 1,548.13 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index gained 0.24 percent to 2,067.38.
Total market volume was a healthy 42 million soles ($17 million) on 2,217 trades. Overall, 44 stocks rose, 24 fell and 26 were flat.
Traders said volume was boosted by two large crosses of Banco Wiese -- 2.1 million shares at 4.03 soles -- and food company Nicolini -- 4.6 million shares at 1.65 sol.
Nicolini accounted for 20.61 percent of total trade and ended down 0.15 percent to 4.03 soles at the close. Wiese accounted for 18.33 percent and ended up 0.33 percent to 1.65 sol.

Among leaders, miner Buenaventura gained 2.27 percent to 22.50 soles on 547,955 shares, while another miner Milpo was up 2.24 percent to 14.58 soles on 161,407 shares and electricity distributor Edelnor increased 0.63 percent to 3.17 soles on 85,538 shares.
"At the close, most of the leaders still had sell orders. That could influence things downwards for Friday's session, although it is not a determining factor," said Elcorobarrutia.
